result.decision_rationale:
The required unit gate passed, and the three round-nine fixes are verified. Two defects remain. Recovery can authenticate a BLOCKED notice using a different comment’s marker. The foreground live log can also leave the owner seeing that Codex is reviewing after launch setup has failed.

## Continuation for Claude

Report these blockers in the enrolled conversation. Round 10 reaches the documented review limit, so further work requires an explicit owner extension. If authorized, bind the unique marker match to the recorded comment ID and report reviewer startup from the confirmed process-start callback. Extend the existing delayed-notice and zero-dispatch fixtures to cover both failures. Keep the correction confined to publication integrity and progress reporting, then run the required unit gate on the corrected candidate through the pinned controller.

The gate log records passes for all four ForegroundRoundTenTests, including the continuing watcher and the foreground request that failed before process creation. The amendment-freshness, pre-exit output, review-accounting and handoff tests also passed.

Read-only Git checks confirmed HEAD, the supplied merge base and identical controller and test sources at 4dfac2d and the candidate. The controller hashes for the three earlier interface demonstrations match their cited Git blobs.

required_gaps: A recovery result showing that the recorded comment itself must be the unique marker match when its body differs by leading whitespace.
A foreground live-log observation from the existing zero-dispatch fixture showing the setup failure and an accurate final status for that attempt.
source_inspection_only: The cross-comment authentication result follows from the raw marker-prefix check, the normalized body comparison and the restoration transaction. The current tests exercise CRLF and ordinary duplicate markers separately.
The gate verifies zero reviewer dispatch and the resulting watch status. The misleading live-log entry on that same path follows from the order of logging, stream setup and exception handling.

findings.actual: The new reuse call checks the normalized body at the recorded ID, but publication_problems only counts the comments that start with the marker. Normalization strips the recorded comment’s leading blank line. The later comment supplies the sole raw marker match. Both checks pass on different comments, so recovery clears restore_needed and leaves the conflicting reason last on the PR.
findings.blocking_rationale: The controller can declare the public budget blocker restored while the latest comment carrying its marker gives the owner a different reason.
findings.expected: The recorded ID, author, complete marker and preserved body must identify the same comment before reuse. A mismatch requires a correction or an explicit integrity stop.
findings.requested_correction: Require the sole marker match to have the recorded comment ID. Compare that comment’s normalized body with the verified outbox body.
findings.requested_evidence: Extend the delayed-notice fixture with a leading blank line on the recorded comment and a conflicting marker match under another ID. Verify correction or an integrity stop, stable behavior on a second resume, and continued reuse for CRLF alone.
findings.title: A different comment can supply the marker for a reused BLOCKED notice
findings.trigger: A delayed BLOCKED notice has been acknowledged and recovery still needs to restore the blocker. The recorded comment acquires a leading blank line before its marker. A later comment by the expected actor starts with that marker and gives a different reason.

findings.actual: review_attempt writes “is reviewing candidate” before CodexReviewer.run opens its streams or creates a process. The setup failure records launched=false and raises before the normal attempt-ended log entry. The last live-log message for the attempt therefore says Codex is reviewing, while the command result and watch report the launch failure.
findings.blocking_rationale: An owner following the documented foreground terminal tail receives a false running status and misses the blocker on that same feed.
findings.expected: The foreground tail distinguishes launch preparation from a confirmed reviewer start and records the setup failure against the affected candidate and attempt.
findings.requested_correction: Emit the running message after process creation is confirmed and append a concise, sanitized failure message when closing a never-launched attempt.
findings.requested_evidence: Extend the existing foreground zero-dispatch fixture to inspect live.log alongside watch and the parsed command result. Verify that all three describe the failed launch accurately and that a successful reviewer still shows activity before exit.
findings.title: The foreground live log reports a reviewer start before process creation
findings.trigger: A foreground review reaches reviewer stream setup and opening its stderr file fails before subprocess creation, as in the candidate’s zero-dispatch fixture.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The same chronological listing now feeds the established publication check. The candidate gate verifies reuse for CRLF alone and a distinct correction for an ordinary competing copy, including repeat recovery. R10-F1 covers a newly exposed case that the former recorded-comment prefix check rejected.

Watch records the attempts already finished at attachment. The continuing-watcher test verifies that an untouched earlier stream first selected after a failed replacement launch stays labeled historical, with the blocker visible.

The status-line fixture verifies both a first request with zero dispatch and a later unlaunched request following an accepted review. Watch identifies the requested candidate separately and preserves the earlier accepted verdict. R10-F2 concerns the separate foreground live log.

Gate and reviewer activity are viewable during execution. Watch now distinguishes historical activity, requested candidates and accepted reviews.
